decision_queue_p0_p2_not_autofixed.desc: Wrong isotonic fit under tied scores: after running PAVA over all rows, fit() collapses duplicate x values by taking fit[last-occurrence], which is the MAXIMUM fitted value within each tie group (fit is non-decreasing and ties are contiguous after the sort). The correct isotonic solution averages y (weighted) within tied x before PAVA (sklearn's _make_unique). Consequences, all empirically verified on this Mac: (1) order-dependence — fit(raw=[0,0], y=[0,1]) predicts p=1.0 while fit(raw=[0,0], y=[1,0]) predicts p=0.5 for identical data; (2) systematic UPWARD bias at tied scores — with 25 distinct scores over 3000 perfectly-calibrated samples, mean bias +0.014, max +0.077 — which is exactly the p-optimism this wave-9 module was written to eliminate (the p feeds the live veto p<0.30 and the size multiplier once META_CALIBRATION_MODE='purged_oof' flips); (3) degenerate catastrophe — constant scores with mixed labels (n=2000, 50% base rate) yield a calibrator with p==1.0 EVERYWHERE, and fit_calibrator happily returns it because it guards np.unique(y)>=2 but never np.unique(scores)>=2. LightGBM scores are sums over discrete leaves, so exact ties are common in practice, especially at the small n_iter the meta booster early-stops to. Not live today (strategy_config.META_CALIBRATION_MODE='legacy'), which is why this is P1 not P0 — but it sits directly on the wave-9 activation path and partially defeats the module's stated purpose.
decision_queue_p0_p2_not_autofixed.fix_sketch: In IsotonicCalibrator.fit, group by unique x FIRST: ux = np.unique(xs); for each tie group compute the weighted mean of y and the summed weight (vectorizable with np.add.reduceat over the searchsorted group boundaries); run _pava on those per-unique-x means/weights; set self.x_=ux, self.y_=clip(pava_result). This is permutation-invariant and matches sklearn IsotonicRegression semantics. decision_queue_p0_p2_not_autofixed.desc: Pooled-panel misuse of the DM test: records are logged K-per-hour across the whole universe (crypto K=6, stocks K=56), pooled across symbols and sorted by ts, yet the Newey-West truncation is h-1 in RECORD units.
